annotation.interpretation_a: A TCP implementation must support urgent data sequences of unlimited length, constrained only by available system resources.
annotation.interpretation_b: A TCP implementation must support urgent data sequences up to the maximum segment size (MSS) or a reasonable upper bound, as any sequence exceeding that is likely an error or attack vector.
annotation.justification: The phrase 'any length' is unbounded. Without a defined upper limit, implementations could reasonably interpret this as either unlimited (subject to system resources) or limited to a practical maximum (e.g., MSS).
annotation.missing_information: The clause does not define a maximum length for the 'any length' sequence of urgent data. This missing constraint affects implementation behavior as it leaves open the question of resource allocation and potential denial-of-service vulnerabilities.
